text: {"votes":[{"issueId":"d0659df4347117af2a5f","verdict":"uphold","severity":4,"reason":"Target: «la civilización tamborilea al borde de la idiocia». Source: «civilization teeters on the brink of idiocy». «Tamborilear» means to drum with the fingers; it never means to wobble or teeter. A Spanish reader hits a wrong verb in the second sentence and reads the whole hook as a translation error, which defeats the 'credible local writer' objective. The fix is trivial («se tambalea») and the image is preserved. Severity 4 is fair because the defect sits in the opening sentence and destroys the comic image rather than merely weakening it.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"033be5af2db37c7bec95","verdict":"uphold","severity":4,"reason":"Same defect as d0659df4347117af2a5f. Target «tamborilea al borde de la idiocia» vs source «teeters on the brink of idiocy». The verb is simply wrong in Spanish. «Idiocia» is attested but «idiotez» is the register the source's dry tone wants; that part is polish, the verb is the blocker.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"7ff8e8babbf3a559bfb3","verdict":"uphold","severity":3,"reason":"Target «revisemos nuestros recibos históricos» calques the slang «let's check our historical receipts». In Spanish «recibos» means only payment slips, so the reader gets an odd image rather than 'check the record'. The policy says idioms are to be recreated, not calqued. I rate 3 rather than 4: the next paragraph immediately delivers the historical evidence, so the argument survives and the damage is credibility and tone, not meaning loss. «Tiremos de hemeroteca» or «repasemos los antecedentes» would carry the same purpose.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"2625792609af24672026","verdict":"uphold","severity":3,"reason":"Same fragment as 7ff8e8babbf3a559bfb3: «revisemos nuestros recibos históricos» for «let's check our historical receipts». Agree with the severity 3 framing here: the calque loses the joke and reads foreign, but the surrounding paragraph makes the intent recoverable. Needs a recreated idiom, not a blocker on its own.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"83cb71404951ce683853","verdict":"uphold","severity":3,"reason":"Target: «cuándo la IA amplifica el aprendizaje frente a cuando lo corta en seco». Source: «when AI amplifies learning versus short-circuits development». The pronoun «lo» can only refer to «aprendizaje», so «desarrollo» disappears from a bolded thesis sentence. It is a real content drift, but the two concepts are close enough that the argument is not inverted, so 3 rather than 4. The second «cuando» is also an indirect interrogative and needs the accent («cuándo»). Both repairs are one-line.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"c7fc5f85354f704e3b4a","verdict":"uphold","severity":3,"reason":"Same fragment as 83cb71404951ce683853. «lo corta en seco» drops «development» from «short-circuits development», and «frente a cuando» lacks the accent on an indirect interrogative. I raise this from 2 to 3 to align with the peer issue: the sentence is bolded as a key takeaway, so losing one of its two objects is more than polish.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"dcf03002302a4c3830ed","verdict":"uphold","severity":4,"reason":"Source frontmatter has «date: 2025-05-31» immediately before «modified: 2025-06-02». Target frontmatter goes straight from «subCategory: Policy» to «modified: 2025-06-02»; the publication date is gone. A date is a factual quantity under the hard constraints, and a missing date can change sorting or publication behaviour. Earlier revision d0530587 kept it, so this is a regression. Deterministic omission, blocks until restored.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"473ab723a2350d38c064","verdict":"uphold","severity":4,"reason":"Duplicate of dcf03002302a4c3830ed. Target lacks the line «date: 2025-05-31» present in the source frontmatter. Factual metadata omission; the fix is to reinsert the line before «modified».","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"005c645f90f4c463efa3","verdict":"uphold","severity":4,"reason":"Duplicate of dcf03002302a4c3830ed and 473ab723a2350d38c064. Source: «date: 2025-05-31 / modified: 2025-06-02». Target: only «modified: 2025-06-02». Agree this is deterministic regardless of whether the site can infer a date from the folder name; the frontmatter value is a preserved factual quantity.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"9fcd8ae6a1cd10ecf3f8","verdict":"reject","severity":1,"reason":"Target has «sourceHash: \"d5356a63e570\"», a 12-character value; the packet's source hash is a 64-character SHA-256. These are plainly different formats, not a stale reference. The history record for this exact candidate reports declaredSourceHash «d5356a63e570» with matchesCurrentSource: true, so the repository's own check accepts it as current. The issue itself concedes the format may differ. Nonblocking; severity 4 is not supported by any textual evidence.","evidenceIds":["target"]},{"issueId":"ee1b3d95ad4538698a01","verdict":"reject","severity":1,"reason":"Same as 9fcd8ae6a1cd10ecf3f8. «sourceHash: \"d5356a63e570\"» is a short-form hash in a different format from the packet's SHA-256, and the pipeline's history entry marks this candidate as matching the current source. No evidence of staleness. The sourceQuote given («date: 2025-05-31») is unrelated to the hash, so the citation does not support the claim.","evidenceIds":["target"]},{"issueId":"6e9f9001426f6853a1d2","verdict":"uphold","severity":2,"reason":"Two claims. (1) Plural: source «The Last to Think» is number-ambiguous in English, and with the subtitle «Human or Machine?» the plural «Los últimos» (humans as the group that thinks last) is a defensible reading; earlier revisions used both. Not a defect. (2) Capitalisation: «Los Últimos en Pensar» / «¿Humano o Máquina?» use English title case; Spanish uses sentence case. That part is valid polish, so I uphold at 2 for the capitalisation only, not the 3 requested.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"f4b0e240229f524a56ba","verdict":"uphold","severity":2,"reason":"Target «title: \"Los Últimos en Pensar\"» and «subTitle: ¿Humano o Máquina?» carry English title case. Spanish convention capitalises only the first word and proper nouns. It signals 'translated' to a native reader on the very first line. Minor polish, one-line fix: «Los últimos en pensar» / «¿Humano o máquina?».","evidenceIds":["target"]},{"issueId":"c3ea62f0f07d6363b888","verdict":"uphold","severity":3,"reason":"Target: «¿Quién se rasga ahora las manos por la pérdida de las habilidades de lectura de mapas?». «Rasgarse las manos» is not a Spanish idiom; it splices «retorcerse las manos» with «rasgarse las vestiduras». Readers see a slip, not style. «la pérdida de las habilidades de lectura de mapas» is a nominal pile-up for the source's quick jab «the loss of map-reading skills now?». Noticeable, not blocking.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"4630562f14e3ca0595f1","verdict":"uphold","severity":3,"reason":"Same fragment as c3ea62f0f07d6363b888: «se rasga ahora las manos» is a non-existent blend of two idioms. Either «se retuerce las manos» (literal hand-wringing) or «se rasga las vestiduras» (recreated idiom) is legitimate; the current hybrid is neither. Agree with 3.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"9fc6af0a025a318f5c6e","verdict":"uphold","severity":2,"reason":"Target «No sea que tengamos que recurrir a la relojería analógica» for «Lest we resort to analog timekeeping». «Relojería» primarily denotes the watch shop or the craft of watchmaking, so the line half-reads as 'go to the watch shop'. The source is deliberately stilted, so a mock-formal register is right; only the noun misfires. Severity 2, not 3: the joke still lands partially and «reloj de agujas» fixes it in one word.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"74ef157163fdf90096d6","verdict":"uphold","severity":2,"reason":"Target: «con estos pánicos —suponiendo que tenga batería. No sea que…». The raya opens an aside and is never closed; Spanish orthography keeps the closing raya even before a full stop, unlike parentheses. The single-dash pattern copies the English em-dash. «Relojería» point is the same as 9fc6af0a025a318f5c6e. Both are minor polish.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"7c734d70524af358f442","verdict":"uphold","severity":2,"reason":"Target «Los años 80 vieron a las calculadoras etiquetadas como «muletas que entorpecerán a una generación»» mirrors «The 1980s saw calculators branded as \"crutches that will hobble a generation.\"». The 'decade saw X' frame is an anglicism, and «entorpecerán» ('will hinder') softens «hobble», breaking the crutch/lameness pair. Valid but polish-level; I do not see the 3 requested since meaning and quotation are intact.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"a40e7cb7a51c3dfb049b","verdict":"uphold","severity":2,"reason":"Same fragment as 7c734d70524af358f442: «Los años 80 vieron a las calculadoras etiquetadas como». Structural anglicism that a local writer would phrase as «En los 80, a las calculadoras se las tachó de…». Agree with severity 2.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]},{"issueId":"b1f24f5cc27733842469","verdict":"reject","severity":2,"reason":"The claim is that the opening was not rewritten and no rationale was documented. But 'Introduction: rewrite' is a structural mode, not a hard constraint, and the objective is credible local writing, not divergence for its own sake. «Cada generación descubre su propio espantajo tecnológico» is idiomatic Spanish with the source's edge intact. The concrete defects in this paragraph («tamborilea», the unclosed raya, «relojería») are already tracked in d0659df4347117af2a5f, 033be5af2db37c7bec95, 74ef157163fdf90096d6 and 9fc6af0a025a318f5c6e. Once those are fixed the intro works as a valid alternative; a full rewrite is optional and should not be listed as a defect.","evidenceIds":["source","target"]}]}
